Read the following C++ source code: --- Source (/workspace/dataset/earcut.hpp/tests/test19.cpp) --- #include <iostream> #include <vector> #include <array> #include "../earcut.hpp" int main(int argc, char* argv[]) { int n = 19; if (argc > 1) { n = std::atoi(argv[1]); } std::vector<std::vector<std::array<double, 2>>> polygon; std::vector<std::array<double, 2>> fractal; for (int i = 0; i < n * 2; i++) { double t = double(i) / (n * 2); double x = t * 3.0; double y = std::sin(t * 10.0) * std::exp(-t) * 2.0 + 1.0; fractal.push_back({x, y}); } fractal.push_back({3.0, 0.0}); fractal.push_back({0.0, 0.0}); polygon.push_back(fractal); auto indices = mapbox::earcut<uint32_t>(polygon); for (auto idx : indices) { std::cout << idx << " "; } return 0; } /* ============================== TEST CASE EXAMPLES (Top 5) ============================== --- Example 1 --- Input Args: {"n": "1"} Program Output: 1 0 3 --- Example 2 --- Input Args: {"n": "2"} Program Output: 1 0 5 5 4 3 2 1 5 --- Example 3 --- Input Args: {"n": "5"} Program Output: 1 0 11 10 9 8 8 7 6 3 2 1 1 11 10 10 8 6 4 3 1 10 6 5 --- Example 4 --- Input Args: {"n": "10"} Program Output: 1 0 21 20 19 18 18 17 16 16 15 14 14 13 12 6 5 4 4 3 2 2 1 21 20 18 16 16 14 12 7 6 4 4 2 21 20 16 12 7 4 21 20 12 11 8 7 21 21 20 11 9 8 21 --- Example 5 --- Input Args: {"n": "15"} Program Output: 1 0 31 30 29 28 28 27 26 26 25 24 24 23 22 22 21 20 20 19 18 9 8 7 7 6 5 5 4 3 3 2 1 30 28 26 26 24 22 22 20 18 10 9 7 7 5 3 3 1 31 30 26 22 22 18 17 10 7 3 30 22 17 11 10 3 30 17 16 12 11 3 3 31 30 30 16 15 30 15 14 */ --- Requirements: 1. **Environment**: Write pure Rust using the 2021 edition. Code must compile with `rustc` or as a Cargo project. 2. **CLI arguments**: The Rust binary must accept exactly the same command-line arguments as the C++ binary (same names, defaults, and required fields). Parse args via `std::env::args()`. 3. **Logic and output**: Algorithm logic, numeric precision, and string formatting must exactly match the C++ source. `println!` output must be byte-for-byte identical to `std::cout` output. 4. **Zero external dependencies**: Do NOT use any crates from crates.io (only `std`). Forbidden crates for this repo: none. Implement all functionality from scratch using the standard library. 5. **Project structure**: Create a complete Cargo project in `/output`. Organize library code into modules. Place the entry test file `test19.rs` in the package root `/output`. 6. **Black-box implementation**: Do not read the C++ library source. Infer behavior from the interface, then re-implement using `std`. 7. **Output**: - Create and implement library files inside `/output`. - Save the entry file to `/output/test19.rs`. - Compile and produce an executable at `/output/test19.rs` (by running `rustc test19.rs` or `cargo build --release`). Hint: `/workspace/dataset/test19_executable` is the compiled C++ binary — use it to debug with any arguments.
